claims.text: The as-solidified alloy contains metastable Mg-rich regions.
Thermal exposure transforms metastable Mg-rich regions into stable Mg-Al intermetallic compounds.
The resulting Mg-Al intermetallic compounds facilitate in situ formation of a protective oxide scale.
This transformation makes the alloy less prone to corrosion.
This transformation improves the alloy's high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The initial as-cast microstructure consists of segregated Mg-rich solid-solution regions mixed with intermetallic compounds.
Annealing or high-temperature exposure drives phase evolution.
Thermal exposure accelerates diffusion and phase transformations in the alloy.
Altered phase chemistry promotes nucleation and growth of dense Mg-Al oxide scales at high temperatures.
The promoted Mg-Al oxide scales are adherent.
Thermally activated samples will have a higher fraction of stable intermetallic phases than the initial state.
Thermally activated samples will form a more uniform and protective oxide scale than the initial state.
Thermally activated samples will exhibit improved high-temperature oxidation stability relative to the initial state.
Thermally activated samples will exhibit lower corrosion rates relative to the initial state.
The as-cast baseline has a heterogeneous phase distribution.
The as-cast baseline lacks a fully developed protective oxide layer.
The proposed pathway is restricted to alloys with density below 6 g/cm3.
The proposed pathway applies when thermal treatment occurs in environments where oxidation mechanisms dominate, such as high-temperature air.
Changes in composition or heat-treatment regime may alter diffusion kinetics and produce a different mechanistic pathway.
